subject.title: Bug: async sessions_send results are not delivered cleanly to Telegram-bound requester session

question: For `sessions_send(..., timeoutSeconds: 0)`, should OpenClaw automatically deliver exactly one final completion to the requester’s bound external channel, or should fire-and-forget results remain internal unless the caller explicitly relays them?
rationale: The current reply-back and announce lifecycle intentionally supports agent coordination, but the reported duplicate/lost Telegram behavior shows that the external-delivery ownership is ambiguous; code alone cannot safely choose which path owns the user-visible completion.

options.title: Exactly-once automatic announce
options.body: Make the A2A lifecycle own one deduplicated final delivery to the requester’s preserved channel/thread while keeping internal wrappers transcript-only.

options.title: Internal fire-and-forget only
options.body: Treat timeout-zero sends as internal dispatch and require the requester agent or an explicit message action to produce any user-visible result.

options.title: Separate explicit mode
options.body: Preserve current behavior temporarily and add a clearly named delivery mode after defining compatibility and migration semantics.

recommendation.title: Exactly-once automatic announce
recommendation.body: Make the A2A lifecycle own one deduplicated final delivery to the requester’s preserved channel/thread while keeping internal wrappers transcript-only.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history most strongly connects this contributor to the shared session-routing and channel-delivery boundary where the contract must be enforced.
